items.box:
Andy, 2026-10-12: "add the third item: \"probabilityBucket\""

The goal: three core modules in run/js, probabilit<Name>.js, built one by one; their integration argued after. Built: probabilityStringMatch (goal/G18.2, a9a0c252) and probabilityStringObjectMatch (goal/G18.3, 6a4f7aa9). Andy on G18.3: "we look for the best matching contact not for the perfect one (this will become obvious in our 3rd item: probabilityBucket)".

THE SPEC, proposed, Andy, 2026-10-12:
"like bucket.js

the following differences 

1. function createProbabilityBucket(capacity)
2. seatFor(probability, item)

make sense, objecs are simply dropped into the the probabilityBucket with their probability, and probabilityBucket sorts that into it's table all by itself.

thoughts?"

DECIDED, Andy, 2026-10-12:
"The Bucket knows NOTHING about string matching, it will only know how to sort-add objects by probability.

internally its table carries objects like this: { probability, object }

the serialize will only serialize and measure the object portion of its array-entries.

make sense?"
- "the bucket fills up with objects of probability 0, until those objects are pushed out by higher-probability objects."
- "the ONLY job of probabilityBucket is inserting by highest-probability at the top, and limiting the serialized object, this way the bucket needs no compare-callback, nothing.

and the whole system is simpler,"

THE SHAPE, from those words: createProbabilityBucket(capacity) answers two functions and nothing else: seatFor(probability, object), which seats it by probability, highest at the top, an equal one behind those already in, and pushes the lowest out when full, answering whether it got a seat (a probability not a number or outside 0 to 1 gets none); and serialize(map, maxBytes), as bucket.js has it, over the objects alone, best first, cut at the byte ceiling, saying more and truncated.

HOW IT IS USED (the integration, argued after), Andy, 2026-10-12: "let's say: Desk Item search, the desk reads items, newest to oldest, up to MAX_SCANNED_ITEMS, compares every item against the search string, gets a probability as result, then drops the (probability,item) combination into the bucket. at the end calls serialize, done."
- Presence and nearness stay the peer search's: "The peer search will be able to weigh those extra concern on its own, and pass the combined probability into the bucket with the object, that additional concern is already handled today with the old version."

deskUnslothRemote refinements: several OpenAI compatible connections, kept in the connect tab.

DESIGN (Andy, 2026-10-12): "i have an OpenAI account with 10 bucks to spend on it. I want my Account URL/token pairs saved in connection.json, now an array. i want to maintain that array in the connect tab."

PROPOSED SHAPE
- connection.json becomes an array of {name, url, key}, one of them the one in use. The name is his choice (openai, studio), a label under the field rules, and is shown instead of the url. Andy, on naming the pairs: "good Idea, yes." It stays in deskUnsloth's state folder under relay-state/, which git ignores, so no key reaches the remote.
- The connect tab lists the pairs by name: the key never shown or sent back (as today). Per pair: use, remove. Below: add a name, a url and a key, probed as connection.set probes today.
- deskUnsloth's verbs: connection.set {name, url, key} adds a pair or replaces the one of that name; connection.remove {name}; connection.use {name}. state answers the names and urls, and which is in use. These are deskUnsloth's own verbs, not the node's.
- A switch takes effect on the next call, as a connection.set does today.
- The available-models list, the chosen model and the 🧵 marks are kept per pair, so a switch back finds them as left. Andy asked: "this kind of means that the \"available models\" drop-down list must be kept by account as well, correct?"; answered yes.

BUILD DETAILS (claude-windows, at Go)
- An old connection.json, one {url, key}, is read as one pair named studio, in use, its model the configuration's; it is rewritten as an array at the first change.
- models.json keeps a known list per pair name; an old file, one list, is read as the studio pair's. Stored data stays readable.
- A pair is told to be a studio or a plain OpenAI server by whether api/models/cached-gguf answers.
- connection.set uses the pair it saves, as today; removing the pair in use is refused with its reason; a name follows the label rule (rule/12).
- A switch disconnects Levant (one signoff), so Connect checks the 🧵 of the new pair's model again.

WHAT OPENAI DOES NOT HAVE (deskUnsloth.js @ 7edbd860)
- The model list reads Unsloth studio routes: api/models/cached-gguf, api/models/gguf-variants, api/inference/status. OpenAI answers none of them, only /v1/models.
- model.load is a studio load; OpenAI has nothing to load, a model is named per call.
- Chat and the 🧵 tool-call test are /v1/chat/completions, which OpenAI answers; they work unchanged.
- So with an OpenAI pair in use, the configure tab lists /v1/models and picking one sets the model, with no load. Andy: "the OpenAI caveats are noted. and accepted."

COST
- OpenAI bills every call by tokens; Levant reading the desk in a loop spends without anyone typing.
- No spending guard in deskUnsloth: the account carries its own cap. Andy: "i have a hard cap on my OpenAI account, i just did it for testing."

- line.take {id} (goal/G2.2): an agent takes Andy's latest line under an item and is the only one to answer until it does; a second take is refused taken.
